title: Textile microfiber shedding prevention
bottleneck: Synthetic textiles shed millions of microfibers per wash, a major source of ocean microplastic, but no fiber treatment yet prevents shedding without ruining fabric hand, breathability, or durability. Tighter weaves and coatings reduce shedding modestly, while truly low-shed synthetics would need redesigned polymers with different surface and fracture properties. Measurement standards for shedding are still being established.
why_it_blocks: Microfibers are among the most pervasive microplastics in water, soil, and even human tissue, and laundry is a primary pathway. Without source-level prevention, the load grows with every wash cycle worldwide, outpacing any cleanup.
current_state: Washing-machine filters and textile pre-treatments capture a fraction of shed fibers, and some brands market lower-shed fabrics. But the fundamental materials fix — a synthetic fiber that does not fragment under mechanical stress — does not yet exist.
